canonical.auditStatus: planned; not bundled with this guide and may not exist in the current snapshot

disclaimer: Not an official DeepSeek standard, not a certification, not a security audit, and not a legal GB/GB-T/GB-Z instrument. The GB analogy is a communication aid only. Certification grades A-D are orthogonal to the three levels.

rules: Depth and evidence are independent; never collapse them into one score.
static is not runtime; runtime is not UI-rendered; not-measured is not a pass.
blocked is not failed; failed needs evidence attributable to the plugin.
Certification grades A-D describe quality, not adoption depth.

levels.label: DSH-ENTRY
levels.question: Can an existing plugin be recognized, installed, and booted on a target DSH line with little or no code change?

gates.check: base + sample compose; inserted row names resolve
evaluatePluginCompatibility admits, or an explicit exact-version exemption applies
real boot() leaves every target row ACTIVE or disabled
when dsh.client exists: exports['./client'] and a package-root row (static)
report carries host version/commit and artifact mtime; expired evidence is stale

selfCheck: record dsh --version, host commit, and artifact mtime
run dsh-plugin-dev check --json (16 static checks, a subset of dsh-plugin-doctor's 33)
for bundles: dsh --profile <name> --dump-config, then boot and read row states
write the claim with level, evidence state, dsh version, commit, and date

levels.label: DSH-FLOW
levels.question: Once installed, can a user install, configure, use, recover, upgrade, and uninstall the plugin without surprises?
selfCheck: throwaway DSH_HOME: add -> dump-config -> remove, no layer or dependency left
toggle enabled/disabled; dump diff is correct and the id is stable
boot with {} and an invalid value (loud failure with a field path)
follow the README as a new user with a five-minute timer and check the error triad
upgrade then rollback; uninstall leaves no layer/dependency/file
exercise normal, missing-service and port-in-use diagnostics
for client plugins test headless, web and client-off

levels.label: DSH-BOOST
levels.question: Does the plugin use Cordis primitives to make development and use measurably cheaper, and is the claimed saving reproducible?
levels.claim: guiding practice recorded as evidence cards, not a badge

practices.check: effects, timers, connections, watchers, and subprocesses return to baseline
required services use inject; optional services use ctx.get; no polling
hot config uses volatile() and does not remount
event modes match; waterfall observers call next()
seams/isolate/group are used only when needed
tool and prompt prefixes are byte-stable; volatile data uses systemPrompt.context
long work uses jobs; parallel calls are bounded; cancellation propagates
bundle/preset differences are expressed in patches; every practice has an evidence card

notClaimed: generalizing one fixture to another workload
selfCheck: pick one LEV and write the card before optimizing the next
run the negative control and record it
record dsh, cordis, Node, and the commit; a number without an anchor is not evidence
